# AgentDock full documentation

AgentDock is a small TypeScript adapter for serving a compiled LangGraph graph
as AgentDock contract events. LangChain and LangGraph own agent construction,
model/tool orchestration, approval middleware, and checkpointing. The
application owns HTTP parsing, authentication, authorization, tool side effects,
and checkpointer lifecycle.

## Install

```bash
npm install @agentdock-ai/agentdock @agentdock-ai/contracts \
  @langchain/core @langchain/langgraph langchain zod
```

Install the provider integration and checkpoint saver your application uses.
The OpenRouter example uses `@langchain/openrouter`.

## Build and serve an agent

```ts
import { agentEventStateSchema, serveAgent } from "@agentdock-ai/agentdock";
import { ChatOpenRouter } from "@langchain/openrouter";
import { MemorySaver } from "@langchain/langgraph";
import { createAgent, tool } from "langchain";
import { z } from "zod";

const weather = tool(
  async ({ city }) => ({ city, forecast: "Sunny" }),
  {
    name: "get_weather",
    description: "Get current weather.",
    schema: z.object({ city: z.string() }),
  },
);

const graph = createAgent({
  model: new ChatOpenRouter({ model: "openai/gpt-4o-mini" }),
  tools: [weather],
  stateSchema: agentEventStateSchema,
  checkpointer: new MemorySaver(),
}).graph;

const runtime = serveAgent(graph);
await runtime.pipe(response, {
  threadId: authorizedThreadId,
  input: { messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Weather in Lahore?" }] },
  context: { userId: authenticatedUser.id },
});
```

Use the same authorized thread ID to resume an interrupt:

```ts
await runtime.pipe(response, {
  threadId: authorizedThreadId,
  context: trustedContext,
  resume: { decisions: [{ type: "approve" }] },
});
```

`MemorySaver` is for local demonstrations. Use a durable LangGraph saver in
production. The application creates and closes that saver. A client-provided
thread identifier must be authorized and mapped to a server-side LangGraph
thread ID before passing it to AgentDock.

## API

- `serveAgent(graph, { recursionLimit? })` creates a runtime.
- `runtime.stream(run)` returns an async iterable of contract events.
- `runtime.pipe(nodeResponse, run)` writes Server-Sent Events.
- `runtime.toResponse(run)` returns a Web `Response` with a cancelable stream.
- `agentEventStateSchema` adds the small checkpointed event fields needed for
  event continuity after an interrupt/resume.
- Contract types and reducers are exported by `@agentdock-ai/contracts` and
  re-exported by `@agentdock-ai/agentdock`.

AgentDock does not provide an `AgentDock` class, model wrapper, tool registry,
session API, agent loop, or checkpoint adapter.

## Migration

Build the graph with LangChain `createAgent` or LangGraph `StateGraph`, configure
tools and provider integrations directly, and pass the compiled graph to
`serveAgent`. Replace AgentDock checkpoint packages with the corresponding
LangGraph checkpointer package. See the migration guide for package mappings.
